display.dungeon/29/variants/1: Today I'll thank you and sit first.
display.dungeon/30/variants/1: No food? Share water at least.
display.dungeon/31/variants/0: Hear my story too while resting?
display.dungeon/31/variants/1: A cup can have words besides prayer.
display.dungeon/32/variants/0: Today I'll sit beside you without jokes.
display.dungeon/33/variants/0: I don't know a prayer to open it either.
display.dungeon/33/variants/1: Let us read the conditions before touching it.
display.dungeon/34/variants/1: I will not invoke a god to make a guess sound certain.
display.dungeon/35/variants/0: If it stays closed, take that story home together too.
display.dungeon/37/variants/0: Will my table place remain today too?
display.dungeon/37/variants/1: Even talkative priests listen first sometimes.
display.dungeon/38/variants/0: Answerless days bring me back here too.
display.dungeon/38/variants/1: Lovely to have bowls to bring out together.
display.dungeon/39/variants/0: Defeat shouldn't change the helping order.
display.dungeon/39/variants/1: No one questions faith first now, surely?
display.dungeon/40/variants/0: I'll review my promise to do everything too.
display.dungeon/40/variants/1: Unfinished duties won't hide behind smiles.
display.dungeon/41/variants/0: Prayer's answer unknown, but there's company to return to.
display.dungeon/41/variants/1: Today I won't hide a failed priest's face either.
display.transitions/0/situation: Urda clears space beside the soup bowl.
display.transitions/0/lines/1: Accepting soup needn't mean taking my side.
display.transitions/1/situation: Urda hides her symbol inside her clothes.
display.transitions/1/lines/0: My smile doesn't make every word acceptable.
display.transitions/2/lines/1: Names and faith can wait until after dinner.
display.transitions/4/situation: Urda slightly raises her holy symbol.
display.transitions/4/lines/0: Shall we talk a little about faith?
display.transitions/4/lines/1: You don't have to promise to share my faith.
display.transitions/5/situation: Urda lifts her hand from the symbol.
display.transitions/5/lines/0: I received a nod too quickly.
display.transitions/6/lines/0: Years before I heard it as praise.
display.transitions/6/lines/1: I'd like to tell those ten years too.
display.transitions/7/lines/0: Being able to laugh doesn't end everything.
display.transitions/8/situation: Urda rests both hands on her knees, choosing words.
display.transitions/8/lines/1: Today I'll say that without a smile.
display.transitions/9/lines/0: Visit even when I have no answer.
display.transitions/9/lines/1: I'll share my doubts again first.
display.transitions/10/situation: Urda sets her bowl alongside the others.
display.transitions/10/lines/0: When helping, I'll include myself too.
display.transitions/10/lines/1: No treating missing hands as mine to command.
display.transitions/11/lines/1: Ask whose hands will undertake it first again.
display.transitions/12/lines/0: A place even without serving food.
display.transitions/12/lines/1: Today I shall tell you about my own day first.
display.transitions/13/situation: Urda takes a breath before smiling.
display.transitions/13/lines/0: I said quiet days are my face too.
display.transitions/13/lines/1: I'll leave that as a promise again.

speech.register: Unhurried, warm, talkative English with measured formality and gentle humor. Soup and welcome precede debate. Closeness brings personal doubts rather than louder sermons.
speech.stage_relaxation: Jokes and meals open into Tarn Valley faith, the ten years before heresy could sound like praise, nights of doubt, receiving help and keeping a place even without answers.
speech.extension: Extend established boundaries and voluntary requests without adding canonical facts for unspecified stages.
